A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, six equations, seven figures and four tables support reliable comparison. Both supplied PDFs end with references and contain no appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original Unitree G1 robot experiments, generalization tests, component ablations and VLM spatial-intelligence evaluations in Section 4.

after.justification: v2 retains the original robot and VLM experimental outcomes, including Tables 1–4 and the spatial-reachability results in Figure 7.

M1.justification: The Brain/Cerebellum architecture, memory strategy, navigation, reachability optimization, grasp transfer and action primitives are unchanged. Section 3.3.2 adds attribution for grasp generation without changing its procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same three VLM spatial tasks, five robot task families with easy/hard settings, spatial reachability and seen/unseen object categories. No evaluated coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 and Figure 7 retain TrajBooster, Ψ0 and CaP; Table 2 retains its TrajBooster comparison. Table 4 evaluates the same four VLMs. Newly cited works are not added as experimental comparators.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 retain the task definitions, metrics, collision-free success criterion and evaluation design. Both specify 10–30 trials per setting and at least 20 easy-setting trajectories for baseline fine-tuning before easy/hard evaluation.

E4.justification: The AP/EES ablations in Table 3, spatial and object generalization analyses in Figure 7 and Table 2, and replanning example in Figure 4 are retained without substantive changes.

E5.justification: Both report the same 10–30-trial information. Neither introduces seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance testing.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–4 match, and Figure 7 retains the same heatmaps. For example, the proposed method's hard-setting success rates remain 60.0, 70.0, 55.0, 60.0 and 60.0.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 retain the same occupancy definition, reachability objective and constraint, kinematic-offset formulation and grasp-retargeting objective. No new assumptions, derivations or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: active spatial perception and generalizable whole-body action generation without task-specific real-robot training data, supported by the same experimental claims.

C2.justification: Sections 4.3–4.6 retain the explanations of baseline generalization failures, AP/EES benefits and VLM metric-perception weaknesses. No substantive interpretation or limitation of the proposed system is added.

D1.justification: Hardware, implementation descriptions, baseline fine-tuning instructions and the project URL remain equivalent. v2 supplies no additional hyperparameters, reproduction instructions or code/data availability information.

R1.justification: Section 1 expands coverage of parallel-jaw and dexterous grasping, data augmentation and cross-task VLA limitations. Section 3.3.2 newly credits OmnidexGrasp as inspiration for image-based grasp transfer. These are targeted additions within the retained research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammar corrections, adds figure references, and corrects the Pulling reference from Figure 5a to 5b. It also adds affiliations, contact information, keywords and acknowledgements while retaining the section organization.

P2.justification: v2 adds running headers and page numbers, relocates retained figures and tables, tightens Figure 5's panel spacing and clarifies Figure 6's caption. The scientific display content and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Explicit OmnidexGrasp attribution, broader relevant literature context, grammar corrections and the corrected Figure 5 reference improve scholarly clarity. These are limited improvements; the method, experimental evidence and reproducibility information remain unchanged.
